svg.text: Algorithm 5 — Fast row algorithm (lazy reduction in O(n^ω) time)
recursion on steps i (leaf i = row n−i+1)

text.tspan: Pad D with an identity block on the right: R = [D | I]. Rows are processed from the bottom up (step i handles row n−i+1).
lft(r) = earliest column (in original order) with its lowest non-zero entry in row r; the identity columns make it always defined.
Step 1, row 8 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 3, 8, e8.
lft(8) = column 3, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 1 ↔ 3.
Pivot (8, 3) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 8 to the right: columns 8, e8 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[1, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
[1] is a leaf, so it returns A₁ = (1): a single pivot column never acts on itself.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ (dark green) leaves row 7 unchanged.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄] (orange) — here the product is zero, nothing changes.
Step 2, row 7 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 6, 7, e7.
lft(7) = column 6, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 2 ↔ 6.
Pivot (7, 6) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 7 to the right: columns 7, e7 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[2, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
Node [1,2] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (2×2, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
[1,2] returns A₁ = I (shown below the tree): the pivot columns of B never added themselves to one another,
so the internal update R̂[C_r, B] ← R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ (dark green) leaves rows 5, 6 unchanged.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Rows 5, 6 now reflect every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [3,4] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 3, row 6 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 8, e6, e8.
lft(6) = column 8, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 3 ↔ 8.
Pivot (6, 8) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 6 to the right: columns e6, e8 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[3, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
[3] is a leaf, so it returns A₁ = (1): a single pivot column never acts on itself.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ (dark green) leaves row 5 unchanged.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Row 5 now reflects every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [4] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 4, row 5 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 1, 7, e5, e6, e7.
lft(5) = column 1, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 4 ↔ 8.
Pivot (5, 1) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 5 to the right: columns 7, e5, e6, e7 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[4, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
Node [3,4] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (2×2, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
Node [1,4] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (4×4, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
[1,4] returns A₁ (below the tree), the cumulative operations among its own pivot columns: column 8 += column 3.
Inside B they were applied only to the rows of B; rows 1, 2, 3, 4 (dark green) have not seen them yet.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] ← R̂[C_r, B] · A₁: one (4×4)(4×4) product replays those operations on rows 1, 2, 3, 4
(dark gray = changed entries). The block now looks as if the pivot columns of B had been reduced in place.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Rows 1, 2, 3, 4 now reflect every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [5,8] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 5, row 4 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 4, 5, 7, e4, e5, e7, e8.
lft(4) = column 4, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 5 ↔ 8.
Pivot (4, 4) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 4 to the right: columns 7, 5, e4, e5, e7, e8 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[5, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
[5] is a leaf, so it returns A₁ = (1): a single pivot column never acts on itself.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ (dark green) leaves row 3 unchanged.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Row 3 now reflects every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [6] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 6, row 3 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 5, 7, e3, e4, e5, e7, e8.
lft(3) = column 5, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 6 ↔ 8.
Pivot (3, 5) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 3 to the right: columns 7, e3, e4, e5, e7, e8 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[6, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
Node [5,6] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (2×2, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
[5,6] returns A₁ (below the tree), the cumulative operations among its own pivot columns: column 5 += column 4.
Inside B they were applied only to the rows of B; rows 1, 2 (dark green) have not seen them yet.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] ← R̂[C_r, B] · A₁: one (2×2)(2×2) product replays those operations on rows 1, 2
(dark gray = changed entries). The block now looks as if the pivot columns of B had been reduced in place.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Rows 1, 2 now reflect every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [7,8] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 7, row 2 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are 2, 7, e2, e3, e5, e6.
lft(2) = column 2, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 7 ↔ 8.
Pivot (2, 2) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 2 to the right: columns 7, e2, e3, e5, e6 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[7, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
[7] is a leaf, so it returns A₁ = (1): a single pivot column never acts on itself.
Internal update R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ (dark green) leaves row 1 unchanged.
Propagate: R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄]. Arrows: each pivot column of B (green) is applied to the orange columns, those
with a recorded multiplier in Λ̂ and a non-zero entry in the dark-green block; ringed entries flip. One product does all of it.
Row 1 now reflects every deferred operation from the rows below (dark gray = changed entries).
The leaves of [8] will therefore see the correct entries when choosing lft.
Step 8, row 1 (green): candidates with their lowest non-zero in this row are e1, e2, e4, e5, e6, e8.
lft(1) = column e1, the earliest in original order. Transpose positions 8 ↔ 9.
Pivot (1, e1) on the anti-diagonal. Clear row 1 to the right: columns e2, e4, e5, e6, e8 lose their entry;
the multipliers are recorded in Λ̂[8, ·] (orange rings) — the column operations themselves are deferred.
Node [7,8] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (2×2, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
Node [5,8] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (4×4, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
Node [1,8] returns T = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂] (8×8, below the tree): green = A₁, light green = A₂,
orange = the deferred operations of B's pivots onto C's pivot columns. This T is the parent's A₁ (or A₂).
All rows reduced: the n pivots form the anti-diagonal of the left block, and every column right of position n is zero.
The root returns T_A = [A₁, A₁·Λ̂[B,C]·A₂; 0, A₂]; U = 2I − Λ and V = U⁻¹ follow from it (Theorem 5.6, Remark 5.7).
Undo the column permutation: R = R̂ · Pᵀ.
Restricted to the first n columns this is exactly the lazy reduction of Algorithm 1 (Theorem 5.5).
Total time O(n^ω); unlike the column algorithm no matrix inversion is needed, only column permutations and products.

svg.text: if i = j: ▷ leaf: row r = n−i+1
k ← lft(r); transpose columns i ↔ k
Λ̂[i, ℓ] ← −R̂[r, ℓ] / R̂[r, i] for ℓ > i
B ← left half, C ← right half; C_r ← rows of C
R̂[C_r, B] ← R̂[C_r, B] · A₁ ▷ internal update
R̂[C_r, B̄] += R̂[C_r, B] · Λ̂[B, B̄] ▷ propagate
